original_test_intent: Create the approved VLAN subinterface on the specified bond and verify its tag, parent relationship and interface state without error or impact to existing bond/management traffic.
original_method: Through the active network manager or supported API, create a uniquely named VLAN on the approved stable bond using the supplied tag and optional MTU/address/routes, verify complete state, then remove or persist only as authorized.
manual_activity: User/network owner supplies and approves bond/tag/trunk/ownership/persistence and rollback; agent may create only the exact approved VLAN and verify it.
required_inputs: Exact bond parent, members and stable state
Unused VLAN ID/interface name and switch allowed-tag/trunk configuration
Optional MTU, IPv4/IPv6 address, routes and bounded peer test
Management/production exclusions, OOB/console, backup/rollback and recovery owner
safety_requirements: Confirm tag/name unused and parent is the approved bond
Exclude management/production collision and verify independent recovery
Use the owning network API and do not replace/delete existing links or routes
Stop on bond instability, route/tag conflict, traffic leakage or access loss
Preserve evidence and remove/persist only as explicitly approved
agent_execution_scope: Collect complete bond/network baseline and validate supplied matrix
Create the exact VLAN through supported ownership and collect state
Run only approved bounded connectivity and restore/persist as directed
Do not invent values, touch unrelated interfaces, auto-delete/reboot/retry or issue verdict

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Mechanically plausible but unsafe and coverage-changing because it uses eth0 rather than the required bond and invents VLAN/IP values.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Create the approved VLAN on the exact bond through its network owner, then collect untruncated ip -d link, bond, address, route and health evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: VLAN-on-bonding creation, reasonable approved tag, no-error criterion and 20/20 timing fields are preserved.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Perform a reversible, ownership-aware bond VLAN change using project-supplied values and complete before/after topology evidence.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds exact parent/tag, switch coordination, management isolation and deterministic lifecycle.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Prevents a simple eth0 VLAN from falsely satisfying the bonding requirement.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Changing a VLAN under the wrong manager can be reverted asynchronously or conflict with bridge/bond configuration; ownership must be authoritative.

project_override_considerations: Project decides whether the VLAN is temporary or persistent and whether address assignment belongs in this creation case; bare creation remains mandatory.
expected_evidence: Creation command/API record and exit status
Full VLAN ID, name, tagged bond parent, MTU and optional address/route state
Removal or persistence result, rollback/recovery notes and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Master clearly requires a VLAN on bonding; DeepSeek's hard-coded eth0 example is an inadequate implementation, not an authority conflict.

blocked_analysis.analysis: Execution awaits project network inputs; static review is complete.

review_improvement: Restores the bonding-parent requirement and makes the VLAN mutation collision-safe, ownership-aware and recoverable.
independent_technical_reasoning: A VLAN subinterface inherits carrier and MTU constraints from its lower device; creating it on eth0 is not equivalent to attaching it to a bond and may bypass redundancy. The tag must also be permitted end-to-end, while interface existence alone only proves local configuration.
